paragraphs: three+one sells liquidity analysis to public finance offices, showing them when and for how long their cash can be put to work. The firm presents itself as an operation created by public officials for public officials.

Its cashVest program produces weekly cash balance projections as a complement to traditional cash-flow forecasting. It gives a consolidated view of how much cash is available and how long each dollar can work before it is needed. Banking services and fees are analyzed to keep the relationship equitable. Marketplace and peer-interest benchmarks are offered so an office can gauge the value of its cash. A dedicated team works on liquidity-management strategy as an objective, third-party data provider.

Published case studies describe county and city finance offices, among them Suffolk County, New York, which the site says began using cashVest to complement its cash-management, finance and audit departments. Another says Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, partnered with the company in 2017. A separate product, the rfpPrep digital portal, is described as a way to issue an investment services RFP. The company also states that it is a national partner of NACo Financial Services Corporation.
